tytul: Whole gooseberries in very light syrup (NCHFP)
wstep: This card describes the NCHFP method for canning whole gooseberries, packed raw in a very light syrup, in a boiling-water bath.

akapity: Use these NCHFP directions only for the berries on its list, which includes gooseberries.
Choose ripe, sweet berries with uniform color.
NCHFP uses on average 8 pounds (about 3.6 kg) of berries for a load of 9 pint jars and 12 pounds (about 5.4 kg) for 7 quart jars.
Wash 1 or 2 quarts (about 0.95–1.9 l) of berries at a time and drain them.
Snip off the heads and tails of the gooseberries with scissors.
NCHFP allows syrup, juice or water as the liquid; this card uses a very light syrup.
Syrup helps keep the flavor, color and shape of the fruit, but it does not prevent spoilage.
NCHFP uses US measures: a cup holds about 237 ml.

For a very light syrup (about 10% sugar) NCHFP uses 6 1/2 cups of water and 3/4 cup of sugar for a load of 9 pint jars, or 10 1/2 cups of water and 1 1/4 cups of sugar for 7 quart jars; heat the water and sugar together to a boil.
NCHFP also gives a hot pack for gooseberries; this card describes only the raw pack.
Pour 1/2 cup of the hot syrup into each clean jar.
Fill the jars with the raw berries, shaking them down gently as you fill.
Cover the berries with hot syrup, leaving 1/2 inch (about 1.3 cm) of headspace.
Put on the lids and process.
At 0–1000 ft (up to 300 m) process pints for 15 minutes and quarts for 20.
Above 1000 ft the food may spoil if the time is not increased.
At 1001–3000 ft (above 300 m up to 900 m) process pints for 20 minutes and quarts for 25.
At 3001–6000 ft (above 900 m up to 1800 m) process pints for 20 minutes and quarts for 30.
Above 6000 ft (above 1800 m) process pints for 25 minutes and quarts for 35.
The card converts feet to metres and rounds the limits down, towards the longer time: 1000 ft becomes 300 m, 3000 ft becomes 900 m and 6000 ft becomes 1800 m.
Shortening the time or cooling jars in cold water can also lead to spoilage.
NCHFP times are for US jar sizes: a pint holds about 473 ml and a quart about 946 ml.
JarAtlas rule (NCHFP does not test metric jars): for a jar of up to 473 ml use the pint time, and for a larger jar of up to 946 ml, for example 0.5 l or 0.9 l, use the quart time.
This NCHFP recipe gives no time for jars larger than a quart, such as 1 l, so JarAtlas recommends smaller jars.
